liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stagger Lee** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it a personal favorite version of the song; Reviewer considers this one of the best versions of Stagger Lee [7][8]
- **Samson and Delilah** (2 reviews): Opens the second set with great energy and charging playing; Jerry plays into shredding territory [7][11]
- **The Promised Land** (1 review): One guitarist repeats the same irritating opening note for about 150 seconds, though the song is brisk and light [6]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Follows nearly four minutes of quiet downtime and is played in a lived-in, experienced way [6]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Named with Stagger Lee as a first-set standout [11]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Pretty, but the second set slows down after Samson; Tennessee Jed was solid but unspectacular [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil's Disco Joke**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Encore Call / Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-05-03.nak700.glassberg.motb.83674.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 165 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd79-05-03.glassberg.vernon.18870.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Detailed audience recording from a sweet spot; Music comes through well, but crowd noise is excessive, preventing high-volume listening [10][11]
- **gd1979-05-03.177539.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 169 min [3]
- **gd1979-05-03.sonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.88851.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: This audience copy is judged better than the other available copies; Very nice audience recording; tapers by then had mastered the craft; Uploader says the ECM-250 recording sounds like a front-of-board recording [5][12][14]

## Around the show

- Phil tells a joke from the stage during the first set [6]
- Show was the band's return east after Keith and Donna left; fans were curious how the new keyboardist would sound [9]
- Hours before the show, a man in a Road Crew jacket handed out containers of Electric Kool-Aid to people in line [9]
- Fans didn't know the keyboardist beforehand; some briefly thought the blond man at the Hammond was Gregg Allman [10]
- Reviewer spent the day outside the Coliseum waiting for doors, then set up about 15 feet from the stage [15]
- Brent's playing is more interesting than Keith's was late in his tenure with the band [8]
- Brent's second show with the band; he gels with them quickly [10]
- The band is still clearly figuring out the new keyboardist; nothing especially special [14]
- The new keyboardist was still finding his place, so Jerry, Bob and Phil carried the improvisation [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-05-03.nak700.glassberg.motb.83674.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and B. Koucky; source: Nakamichi CM700's > Sony 158SD > MAC [1]
- **gd79-05-03.glassberg.vernon.18870.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; source: Audience Recording [2]
- **gd1979-05-03.177539.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Barry Glassberg's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell UDXL II) [3]. Also: Fresh transfer by Bob Menke from Glassberg's master cassettes, coordinated by Charlie Miller, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; A Sony ECM-250 source supplies short patches in Playin' In The Band (0:41) and Drums (0:16) [3]
- **gd1979-05-03.sonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.88851.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [5]. Also: Sony ECM-250 tapes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; patches from the Glassberg Nakamichi 700 source, pitch adjusted to match [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1979-05-03 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1979-05-03-backstage-pass/) [19]
